fieldissues.issue: The opening attribution ends with “according to” and then starts a new sentence fragment, leaving the source attribution unfinished.
The title describes a voter-intimidation goal as established, while the medium and long say the supplied notes do not show the campaign’s reach or whether intimidation occurred.

proposedchanges.change: Repair the opening as: “Less than two days after Trump told the Proud Boys to ‘stand by,’ the group launched an automated text-message campaign seeking recruits, according to the supplied account.” Then retain the following sentence’s limits on reach and completed intimidation.
Use an attributed title such as: “Proud Boys text campaign seeks recruits for alleged voter-intimidation effort.”

evidencebasis: The supplied medium and long describe a recruitment message, say the source attribution is limited, and state that reach and participation are unknown. The Trump File URL is retained.
notes: Existing entry-3026. The category fits the election context; repair the incomplete attribution and keep the outcome uncertain.

fieldissues.issue: “Election Interference,” “Democratic Institution Undermining,” election-pressure, and democratic-norm tags do not describe a proposal to restrict birthright citizenship that Trump did not issue.

proposedchanges.change: Use a citizenship or immigration-policy category if available, with wording that identifies a proposal rather than a policy in effect. Replace the election labels with “birthright citizenship,” “Fourteenth Amendment,” “proposed executive order,” and “William Barr.”

evidencebasis: The supplied medium and long say Trump considered an order, Barr reportedly opposed it, no order was issued, and citizenship rules remained unchanged. The Trump File URL is retained.
notes: Existing entry-3037. The title and descriptions already distinguish the proposal from an enacted policy.

fieldissues.issue: “Over 50,000 Facebook group posts” may count phrase occurrences as distinct posts. The long description cites about 41,000 instances of tracked phrases plus other expressions and warns categories may overlap.
War and Iran labels do not describe violent political rhetoric in public Facebook groups before the 2020 election.

proposedchanges.change: Replace the unqualified count with: “Analysis finds widespread violent rhetoric in public Facebook groups before 2020 election.” If keeping a number, define whether it counts posts, phrase instances, or overlapping categories.

Use the existing “Violent Rhetoric / Threats” category and “Political Violence / Threats” subcategory if applicable. Replace war tags with “Facebook groups,” “violent rhetoric,” “election outcome,” and “CounterAction analysis.”

evidencebasis: The supplied long description distinguishes phrase instances from unique users or plans, says categories may overlap, and does not establish campaign coordination. The Trump File URL is retained.
notes: Existing entry-3048. Keep the analysis method and limits visible when presenting any total.

fieldissues.issue: Donald Trump and the election-category labels repeat people and category metadata instead of naming the specific false ballot claim and local correction.

proposedchanges.change: Replace the duplicated person/category labels with “Virginia Beach sample ballots,” “Eric Trump video,” “2020 vote-counting,” and “false ballot-destruction claim.”

evidencebasis: The supplied medium and long say Virginia Beach officials identified the papers as sample ballots and that reporting did not establish burned official ballots or an effect on election results. Both URLs are retained.
notes: Existing entry-3059. The title, medium, and long distinguish the video’s claim from officials’ identification of the papers.

fieldissues.issue: “Sexual Assault Confession” and “Predator Normalization” treat recorded remarks as an adjudicated crime and a settled psychological conclusion. The supplied medium says the recording documents speech but does not adjudicate every allegation or establish a conviction.
The long description repeatedly calls the recording a systematic assault confession and adds conclusions about impunity, consent, and motive beyond the supplied medium’s careful account.
The subcategory and several tags repeat those legal and psychological conclusions.

proposedchanges.change: Replace with: “Access Hollywood recording captures Trump’s comments about kissing and grabbing women.”

Rewrite from the documented recording and public response. Quote the relevant remarks, identify the recording’s 2016 release and Trump’s apology if retained from the supplied medium, and distinguish public criticism from any legal finding or separate allegation.

Use a category for sexual misconduct statements or consent controversy if available. Replace “confession” and “predatory behavior normalization” labels with “Access Hollywood recording,” “2005 remarks,” “consent,” and “2016 campaign.”

evidencebasis: The supplied medium describes the recorded remarks, their release during the 2016 campaign, and Trump’s apology, while expressly distinguishing speech from adjudicated allegations. The Washington Post and Wikipedia URLs are retained.
notes: Existing entry-307. Keep the recorded words distinct from legal conclusions about conduct.

fieldissues.issue: “Human Rights Violations,” “Immigration Crackdown,” and deportation tags do not describe GSA’s delay in authorizing resources for Biden’s transition.
The list is null although GSA and the Presidential Transition Act are central to the supplied account.

proposedchanges.change: Use an election-transition or government-accountability category if available. Replace immigration labels with “presidential transition,” “GSA authorization,” “orderly transfer of power,” and “2020 election certification.”
Add “General Services Administration” and “Biden transition team.”

evidencebasis: The supplied medium and long give the November 23 authorization date, the resources delayed, and the effect on preparation time, while saying the public record does not show Trump directly ordered Murphy’s decision. Both URLs are retained.
notes: Existing entry-3080. The long description separates the documented delay from the unproven claim that Trump directed it.

fieldissues.issue: “Caught using Facebook to push election lies to 2.45 million followers” implies Bannon directed every post and that all followers received or believed the material. The long description says neither is established.
The existing specific topics are useful, but they do not identify the combined follower count as page reach rather than unique viewers.

proposedchanges.change: Replace with: “Facebook removes seven election-related pages associated with Steve Bannon.” If the audience number is kept, describe it as the pages’ combined follower count.
Retain “Facebook page removal,” “coordinated inauthentic behavior,” “election misinformation,” and “2020 election”; do not imply 2.45 million unique viewers or people persuaded.

evidencebasis: The supplied medium and long say the pages had a combined follower count above 2.45 million and that Facebook cited inauthentic behavior; they do not establish unique reach, Bannon’s direction of every post, or an election effect. Both URLs are retained.
notes: Existing entry-3091. The long description is appropriately cautious; align the headline with its attribution and reach limits.

fieldissues.issue: “donald trump,” “national security violations,” and “war / militarization” repeat the person or broad category rather than the reported question about a possible strike and advisers’ response.

proposedchanges.change: Replace the repeated person/category labels with “Iran strike options,” “November 2020,” “Mike Pence,” “Mike Pompeo,” and “military transition.”

notes: Existing entry-3101. The category fits the war-policy subject; the topic tags should identify the specific event.

Donald Trump and election-category labels repeat the person/category rather than the Pennsylvania appeal, certification, and court ruling.

Replace duplicated person/category labels with “Pennsylvania certification,” “Third Circuit appeal,” “2020 election challenge,” and “court rejects unsupported claims.”
